title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
What is Vaccine Effectiveness?


Measures how well a vaccine performs in real-world settings


Different from vaccine efficacy measured in trials


Usually expressed as a percentage reduction in risk


Important for public health decision making

title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
Image of vaccine




Covid vaccine


Vaccination remains one of the most effective public health interventions ever developed. Vaccines reduce the risk of infection, severe illness, hospitalisation, and death by helping the immune system recognise and respond to specific pathogens. Large-scale vaccination programmes have contributed to the control or elimination of diseases such as smallpox, polio, and measles in many parts of the world.


During outbreak investigations, vaccination status is often an important variable for understanding patterns of disease transmission. By comparing infection rates among vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals, public health professionals can estimate vaccine effectiveness and assess whether additional interventions may be required. These findings support evidence-based decision making and help guide vaccination policy and practice.

title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
Why Does Vaccine Effectiveness Matter?


Supports vaccination policy


Helps evaluate programme success


Identifies groups needing additional protection


Supports outbreak response

title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
Outbreak Investigation Example


A measles outbreak occurred in a secondary school.


Investigators compared infection rates among vaccinated and unvaccinated students.


The results were used to estimate vaccine effectiveness.


Findings informed public health action.

title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
Calculating Vaccine Effectiveness


VE = (1 − Relative Risk) × 100


Relative Risk = attack rate vaccinated ÷ attack rate unvaccinated


Higher VE indicates greater protection


Commonly used during outbreak investigations

title: Introduction to Vaccine Effectiveness
text:
Key Messages


Vaccine effectiveness measures real-world protection


VE supports evidence-based decision making


Outbreak investigations provide useful VE estimates


Interpretation requires consideration of study design
